readings.title: Hagar and Ishmael Sent Away
readings.text: [Genesis 21:8] And the child grew and was weaned. And Abraham made a great feast on the same day that Yitsḥaq was weaned. [9] And Sarah saw <dn>את</dn> the son of Hag̱ar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking. [10] Therefore she said to Abraham, “Drive out this female servant and <dn>את</dn> her son, for the son of this female servant shall not inherit with my son, with Yitsḥaq.” [11] And the matter was very evil in the eyes of Abraham because of his son. [12] But <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Abraham, <dq>“Let it not be evil in your eyes because of the boy and because of your female servant. Whatever Sarah has said to you, listen to her voice, for in Yitsḥaq your seed is called.</dq> [13] <dq>“And of <dn>את</dn> the son of the female servant <dn>I</dn> also make a nation, because he is your seed.”</dq> [14] And Abraham rose early in the morning, and took bread and a skin of water, and put it on the shoulder of Hag̱ar, giving it and <dn>את</dn> the boy to her, and sent her away. And she left and wandered in the Wilderness of Be’ĕrsheḇa. [15] And the water in the skin was used up, and she placed <dn>את</dn> the boy under one of the shrubs. [16] And she went and sat down by herself a distance of about a bowshot, for she said, “Let me not see the death of the boy.” And she sat opposite him, and lifted up her voice and wept. [17] And <dn>Elohim</dn> heard <dn>את</dn> the voice of the youth. And the <dn>Messenger of Elohim</dn> called to Hag̱ar from the heavens, and said to her, <dq>“What is the matter with you, Hag̱ar? Do not fear, for <dn>Elohim</dn> has heard the voice of the youth where he is.</dq> [18] <dq>“Arise, lift up <dn>את</dn> the youth and hold him with <dn>את</dn> your hand, for <dn>I</dn> make a great nation of him.”</dq> [19] And <dn>Elohim</dn> opened <dn>את</dn> her eyes, and she saw a well of water. And she went and filled <dn>את</dn> the skin with water, and gave <dn>את</dn> the youth a drink. [20] And <dn>Elohim</dn> was <dn>את</dn> with the youth, and he grew and dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer. [21] And he dwelt in the Wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.

readings.title: Covenant with Abimelek
readings.text: [Genesis 21:22] And it came to be at that time that Aḇimeleḵ and Piḵol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham, saying, “<dn>Elohim</dn> is with you in all that you do. [23] “And now, swear to me by <dn>Elohim</dn> here that you do not be false to me or to my offspring or to my posterity. According to the kindness that I have done to you, you do to me and to the land in which you have sojourned.” [24] And Abraham said, “I swear.” [25] And Abraham reproved <dn>את</dn> Aḇimeleḵ because of a well of water which Aḇimeleḵ’s servants had seized. [26] And Aḇimeleḵ said, “I do not know who has done <dn>את</dn> this thing, neither did you tell me, nor have I heard of it until today.” [27] And Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Aḇimeleḵ, and the two of them made a covenant. [28] And Abraham set <dn>את</dn> seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves. [29] And Aḇimeleḵ said to Abraham, “What is the meaning of these seven ewe lambs which you have set by themselves?” [30] And he said, “You take <dn>את</dn> these seven ewe lambs from my hand, that they be my witness that I have dug this well.” [31] Therefore he called that place Be’ĕrsheḇa, because the two of them swore an oath there. [32] Thus they made a covenant at Be’ĕrsheḇa. And Aḇimeleḵ rose with Piḵol, the commander of his army, and they returned to the land of the Philistines. [33] And Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Be’ĕrsheḇa, and there called on the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Everlasting Ěl</dn>. [34] And Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines many days.

readings.title: The Binding of Isaac
readings.text: [Genesis 22:1] And it came to be after these events that <dn>Elohim</dn> tried <dn>את</dn> Abraham, and said to him, <dq>“Abraham!”</dq> And he said, “Here I am.” [2] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Take now <dn>את</dn> your son, <dn>את</dn> your only son <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriyah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains of which <dn>I</dn> shall tell you.”</dq> [3] And Abraham rose early in the morning and saddled <dn>את</dn> his donkey, and took <dn>את</dn> two of his young men with him, and <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq his son. And he split the wood for the burnt offering, and arose and went to the place of which <dn>Elohim</dn> had told him. [4] On the third day Abraham lifted his eyes and saw <dn>את</dn> the place from a distance. [5] And Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey while the boy and I go over there and worship, and come back to you.” [6] And Abraham took <dn>את</dn> the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Yitsḥaq his son, and he took <dn>את</dn> the fire in his hand, and <dn>את</dn> a knife, and the two of them went together. [7] And Yitsḥaq spoke to Abraham his father and said, “My father!” And he said, “Here I am, my son.” And he said, “See, the fire and the wood! But where is the lamb for a burnt offering?” [8] And Abraham said, “My son, <dn>Elohim</dn> does provide for <dn>Himself</dn> the lamb for a burnt offering.” And the two of them went together. [9] And they came to the place of which <dn>Elohim</dn> had told him. And Abraham built <dn>את</dn> an altar there and placed <dn>את</dn> the wood in order. And he bound <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq his son and laid <dn>את</dn> him on the altar, upon the wood. [10] And Abraham put out <dn>את</dn> his hand and took <dn>את</dn> the knife to slay his son. [11] But the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> called to him from the heavens and said, <dq>“Abraham, Abraham!”</dq> And he said, “Here I am.” [12] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Do not lay your hand on the boy, nor touch him. For now I know that you fear <dn>Elohim</dn>, seeing you have not withheld <dn>את</dn> your son, <dn>את</dn> your only son, from <dn>Me</dn>.”</dq> [13] And Abraham lifted <dn>את</dn> his eyes and looked, and saw behind him a ram caught in a thicket by its horns. And Abraham went and took <dn>את</dn> the ram, and offered it up for a burnt offering instead of his son. [14] And Abraham called the name of the place, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH Yireh</dn>,’ as it is said to this day, “On the mountain <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> provides.” [15] And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> called to Abraham a second time from the heavens, [16] and said, <dq>“By <dn>Myself</dn> <dn>I</dn> have sworn, declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because you have done <dn>את</dn> this, and have not withheld <dn>את</dn> your son, <dn>את</dn> your only son,</dq> [17] <dq>that <dn>I</dn> shall certainly bless you, and <dn>I</dn> shall certainly increase your seed as the stars of the heavens and as the sand which is on the seashore, and let your seed possess <dn>את</dn> the gate of their enemies.</dq> [18] <dq>“And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed, because you have obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice.”</dq> [19] And Abraham returned to his young men, and they rose and went together to Be’ĕrsheḇa. And Abraham dwelt at Be’ĕrsheḇa. [20] And it came to be after these events that it was reported to Abraham, saying, “See, Milkah also has borne children to your brother Naḥor: [21] “<dn>את</dn> Uts his first-born, and <dn>את</dn> Buz his brother, and <dn>את</dn> Qemu’ĕl the father of Aram, [22] “and <dn>את</dn> Keseḏ, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥazo, and <dn>את</dn> Pildash, and <dn>את</dn> Yiḏlaph, and <dn>את</dn> Bethu’ĕl.” [23] And Bethu’ĕl brought forth <dn>את</dn> Riḇqah. These eight Milkah bore to Naḥor, Abraham’s brother. [24] And his concubine, whose name was Re’umah, also bore <dn>את</dn> Teḇaḥ, and <dn>את</dn> Gaḥam, and <dn>את</dn> Taḥash, and <dn>את</dn> Ma‛aḵah.

readings.title: Sarah's Death and Burial
readings.text: [Genesis 23:1] And the life of Sarah was one hundred and twenty-seven years – the years of the life of Sarah. [2] And Sarah died in Qiryath Arḇa, that is Ḥeḇron, in the land of Kena‛an. And Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her. [3] And Abraham rose up from before his dead, and spoke to the sons of Ḥĕth, saying, [4] “I am a foreigner and a sojourner among you. Give me property for a burial site among you, so that I bury my dead from before me.” [5] And the sons of Ḥĕth answered Abraham, saying to him, [6] “Hear us, my master: You are a prince of <dn>Elohim</dn> among us. Bury <dn>את</dn> your dead in the choicest of our burial sites. None of us withholds from you his burial site, from burying your dead.” [7] And Abraham rose and bowed himself to the people of the land, the sons of Ḥĕth. [8] And he spoke with them, saying, “If it is your desire that I bury <dn>את</dn> my dead from before me, hear me, and approach Ephron son of Tsoḥar for me, [9] and let him give me <dn>את</dn> the cave of Mak̄pelah which he has, which is at the end of his field. Let him give it to me for the full price, as property for a burial site among you.” [10] And Ephron was sitting among the sons of Ḥĕth. And Ephron the Ḥittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Ḥĕth, all who entered at the gate of his city, saying, [11] “No, my master, hear me: I give you <dn>את</dn> the field and the cave that is in it, I give it to you. In the presence of the sons of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead!” [12] And Abraham bowed himself down before the people of the land. [13] And he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying, “If only you would hear me. I shall give the amount of money for the field. Take it from me and let me bury <dn>את</dn> my dead there.” [14] And Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him, [15] “My master, hear me: the land is worth four hundred sheqels of silver. What is that between you and me? So bury <dn>את</dn> your dead.” [16] And Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed out <dn>את</dn> the silver for Ephron which he had named in the hearing of the sons of Ḥĕth, four hundred sheqels of silver, currency of the merchants. [17] Thus the field of Ephron which was in Mak̄pelah, which was before Mamre, the field and the cave which was in it, and all the trees that were in the field, which were within all the surrounding borders, were established, [18] as the property of Abraham in the presence of the sons of Ḥĕth, before all who went in at the gate of his city. [19] And after this Abraham buried <dn>את</dn> Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Mak̄pelah, before Mamre, that is Ḥeḇron, in the land of Kena‛an. [20] Thus the field and the cave that is in it were established to Abraham as property for a burial site by the sons of Ḥĕth.

readings.title: The Death of Terah
readings.text: [Genesis 11:32] And the days of Teraḥ came to be two hundred and five years, and Teraḥ died in Ḥaran.

readings.title: A Wife for Isaac
readings.text: [Genesis 24:1] And Abraham was old, advanced in age. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had blessed <dn>את</dn> Abraham in all that he did. [2] And Abraham said to the oldest servant of his house, who ruled over all that he had, “Please, put your hand under my thigh, [3] and I make you swear by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the heavens and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the earth, that you do not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Kena‛anites, among whom I dwell, [4] but go to my land and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son Yitsḥaq.” [5] And the servant said to him, “What if the woman refuses to follow me to this land? Do I then take <dn>את</dn> your son back to the land from which you came?” [6] And Abraham said to him, “Guard yourself, lest you take <dn>את</dn> my son back there. [7] “<dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of the heavens, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my relatives, and who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, <dq>‘To your seed I give <dn>את</dn> this land,’</dq> <dn>He</dn> sends <dn>His</dn> messenger before you, and you shall take a wife for my son from there. [8] “And if the woman refuses to follow you, then you shall be released from this oath. Only, do not take <dn>את</dn> my son back there.” [9] So the servant put <dn>את</dn> his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and swore to him concerning this matter. [10] And the servant took ten of his master’s camels and left, for all his master’s goods were in his hand. And he arose and went to Aram Naharayim, to the city of Naḥor. [11] And he made his camels kneel down outside the city by a well of water at evening time, the time when women go out to draw water. [12] And he said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>Elohim</dn> of my master Abraham, please meet with me this day, and show kindness to my master Abraham. [13] “See, I am standing by the well of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water. [14] “Now let it be that the young woman to whom I say, ‘Please let down your jar that I may drink,’ and she says, ‘Drink, and let me water your camels too,’ let her be the one <dn>You</dn> have appointed for <dn>Your</dn> servant Yitsḥaq. And by this let me know that <dn>You</dn> have shown kindness to my master.” [15] And it came to be, before he had finished speaking, that see, Riḇqah, who was born to Bethu’ĕl, son of Milkah, the wife of Naḥor, Abraham’s brother, came out with her jar on her shoulder. [16] And the young woman was very good-looking, a maiden, no man having known her. And she went down to the well, filled her jar, and came up. [17] And the servant ran to meet her and said, “Please let me drink a little water from your jar.” [18] And she said, “Drink, my master.” And she hurried and let her jar down to her hand, and gave him a drink. [19] And when she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “Let me draw water for your camels too, until they have finished drinking.” [20] And she hurried and emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well to draw water, and drew for all his camels. [21] And the man was acting silently, wondering whether <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had made his journey prosperous or not. [22] And it came to be, when the camels had finished drinking, that the man took a golden nose ring weighing half a sheqel, and two bracelets for her wrists weighing ten sheqels of gold, [23] and said, “Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room in your father’s house for us to spend the night?” [24] And she said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethu’ĕl, Milkah’s son, whom she bore to Naḥor.” [25] And she said to him, “We have both straw and fodder enough, and room to spend the night.” [26] And the man bowed his head and worshipped <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [27] And he said, “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken <dn>His</dn> kindness and <dn>His</dn> truth toward my master. As for me, being on the way, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> led me to the house of my master’s brothers.” [28] And the young woman ran and told her mother’s house <dn>את</dn> these matters. [29] Now Riḇqah had a brother whose name was Laḇan, and Laḇan ran out to the man by the well. [30] And it came to be, when he saw <dn>את</dn> the nose ring, and <dn>את</dn> the bracelets on his sister’s wrists, and when he heard <dn>את</dn> the words of his sister Riḇqah, saying, “Thus the man spoke to me,” that he went to the man. And see, he stood by the camels at the well. [31] And he said, “Come in, O blessed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! Why do you stand outside? For I myself have prepared the house, and a place for the camels.” [32] And the man came into the house. And he unloaded the camels, and provided straw and fodder for the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him. [33] And food was set before him to eat, but he said, “I do not eat until I have spoken my word.” And he said, “Speak on.” [34] And he said, “I am Abraham’s servant. [35] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed my master exceedingly, and he has become great. And <dn>He</dn> has given him sheep and cattle, and silver and gold, and male and female servants, and camels and donkeys. [36] “And Sarah my master’s wife bore a son to my master when she was old, and to him he has given <dn>את</dn> all that he has. [37] “And my master made me swear, saying, ‘Do not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Kena‛anites, in whose land I dwell, [38] but go to my father’s house and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son.’ [39] “And I said to my master, ‘What if the woman does not follow me?’ [40] “And he said to me, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, before whom I walk, sends <dn>His</dn> messenger with you and shall prosper your way, and you shall take a wife for my son from my relatives and from my father’s house. [41] ‘Then you are released from this oath when you go to my relatives. And if they do not give her to you, then you are released from my oath.’ [42] “And I came today to the well and said, ‘O <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of my master Abraham, if <dn>You</dn> are now prospering the way in which I go, [43] see, I am standing by the well of water, and it shall be that the young woman who comes out to draw water, and to whom I say, “Please give me a little water from your jar to drink,” [44] and she says to me, “Drink, and I also draw for your camels,” let her be the woman whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has appointed for my master’s son.’ [45] “Before I finished speaking in my heart, then see, Riḇqah came out with her jar on her shoulder, and she went down to the well and drew water. And I said to her, ‘Please let me drink.’ [46] “And she hurried and let her jar down from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and let me water your camels too.’ So I drank, and she watered the camels too. [47] “And I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ And she said, ‘The daughter of Bethu’ĕl, Naḥor’s son, whom Milkah bore to him.’ And I put the nose ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists. [48] “And I bowed my head and worshipped <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and blessed <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of my master Abraham, who had led me in the true way to take <dn>את</dn> the daughter of my master’s brother for his son. [49] “And now, if you are to show kindness and truth to my master, tell me. And if not, tell me, so that I turn to the right hand or to the left.” [50] And Laḇan and Bethu’ĕl answered and said, “The matter comes from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, we are unable to speak to you good or evil. [51] “See, Riḇqah is before you, take her and go, and let her be your master’s son’s wife, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken.” [52] And it came to be, when Abraham’s servant heard <dn>את</dn> their words, that he bowed himself toward the earth to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [53] And the servant brought out objects of silver and objects of gold, and garments, and gave them to Riḇqah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and to her mother. [54] And he and the men who were with him ate and drank and spent the night. And they rose up in the morning, and he said, “Send me away to my master.” [55] And her brother and her mother said, “Let the young woman stay with us a few days, at least ten. After that she goes.” [56] And he said to them, “Do not delay me, since <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has prospered my way. Send me away so that I go to my master.” [57] And they said, “Let us call the young woman and ask her.” [58] So they called Riḇqah and said to her, “Would you go with this man?” And she said, “I go.” [59] So they sent away <dn>את</dn> Riḇqah their sister and <dn>את</dn> her nurse, and <dn>את</dn> Abraham’s servant and his men. [60] And they blessed Riḇqah and said to her, “Our sister, become the mother of thousands of ten thousands, and let your seed possess <dn>את</dn> the gate of those who hate them.” [61] And Riḇqah and her young women rose up and rode on the camels and followed the man. So the servant took <dn>את</dn> Riḇqah and left. [62] And Yitsḥaq came from the way of Be’ĕr Laḥai Ro’i, for he dwelt in the land of the South. [63] And Yitsḥaq went out to meditate in the field in the evening. And he lifted his eyes and looked, and saw camels coming. [64] And Riḇqah lifted <dn>את</dn> her eyes, and she saw <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq, and she dismounted from her camel, [65] and said to the servant, “Who is this man walking in the field to meet us?” And the servant said, “It is my master.” So she took a veil and covered herself. [66] And the servant told Yitsḥaq <dn>את</dn> all the matters he had done. [67] And Yitsḥaq brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent. And he took <dn>את</dn> Riḇqah and she became his wife, and he loved her. Thus Yitsḥaq was comforted after his mother’s death.
